note: First visit per session: two spoken sentences. {what it is}. {what ants do here}.

surface.line1: This is the sunny foraging ground outside the nest.
surface.line2: Worker ants cut leaf pieces here and carry them home.

invasion.line1: This clearing is where strangers sometimes try to enter.
invasion.line2: Soldier ants rush out, face them bravely, and send them away.

entrance.line1: This is the nest doorway, busy with ants coming and going.
entrance.line2: They follow scent trails so everyone knows which way to walk.

outpost.line1: This is the soldier outpost by the defensive tunnel.
outpost.line2: Big soldier ants wait here, ready to protect the colony.

garden_a.line1: This is a fungal garden, the colony's underground farm.
garden_a.line2: Gardeners feed the fungus with leaf bits and keep it healthy.

garden_b.line1: This is another garden room where many jobs meet.
garden_b.line2: Different ants share the work so the whole nest stays fed.

hygiene.line1: This is a tidy garden corner for keeping the fungus clean.
hygiene.line2: Tiny helpers fight mold so the food garden stays safe.

nursery.line1: This is the nursery, where baby ants grow.
nursery.line2: Nurse ants feed the larvae and tuck them carefully.

pupae.line1: This is the quiet pupa room next to the nursery.
pupae.line2: Babies rest in cocoons here until they become grown ants.

queen.line1: This is the queen's chamber, the heart of the nest.
queen.line2: The queen lays eggs, and nurses carry them to the nursery.

dump.line1: This is the refuse dump, the nest's cleanup room.
dump.line2: Workers bring old bits and waste here to keep gardens clean.

deep.line1: This is a deep tunnel, a quiet corner of the nest.
deep.line2: Ants explore these passages and learn how the colony is built.
